---
title: "Technical details"
---

This page explains how the site is put together. It is a Quarto website
built with [altdoc](https://altdoc.etiennebacher.com/), with some extra
styling and JavaScript to make it look like a [pkgdown](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/)
(Bootstrap 5) site.

The only file a package keeps in `altdoc/` is `altdown.yml`. Everything else
there is written by `altdown::build_site()` on every build, and gitignored:

```text
altdoc/
├── altdown.yml                # configuration, edited by hand
├── quarto_website.yml         # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.md                   # home page
├── reference.qmd              # function reference index
├── authors.qmd                # authors and citation page
├── altdown.scss               # pkgdown-style theme on top of Quarto's HTML
├── altdown-header.html        # dark-mode default
└── altdown-after-body.html    # navbar alignment, see below
```

## Why generate files?

For a Quarto backend, the intended approach is to modify the source files with a script and then
call `altdoc::render_docs()` yourself (see altdoc's
[customization vignette](https://altdoc.etiennebacher.com/articles/customize.html)).

That is what `build_site()` does. altdoc copies `altdoc/` into its Quarto
project, so files written there before `altdoc::render_docs()` end up in the
site. The main ones are explained below.

### The home page

altdoc's home page is an `index.md` that includes `README.md`. Since altdoc
copies `altdoc/` into its Quarto project after importing the README,
`build_site()` writes its own `altdoc/index.md` to replace it: the README with
a `.column-margin` sidebar, matching pkgdown's layout, with the README's badges
moved into it. `README.md` itself is never modified.

### The reference index

altdoc does not currently have a `_pkgdown.yml`-style `reference:` field for
controlling how the function index is grouped and ordered
([etiennebacher/altdoc#326](https://github.com/etiennebacher/altdoc/issues/326)).

So `altdoc/altdown.yml` has a `reference:` field, using the same basic
structure as pkgdown's. `build_site()` uses it together with the `\name{}` and
`\alias{}` entries in `man/*.Rd` to generate `altdoc/reference.qmd`.

### The navbar and footer

`altdoc/quarto_website.yml` is generated in full: the navbar links the "Get
started" vignette, the reference index, the other vignettes under "Articles"
and the changelog, and the footer has the "Developed by <authors>." text used
by pkgdown, based on `Authors@R`. A `quarto:` field in `altdown.yml` is merged
over it.

## Matching the pkgdown look

`altdown.scss` is a Quarto theme layer:

```yaml
theme: [default, altdown.scss]
```

It is based on pkgdown's own `pkgdown.scss`, but the selectors have been
adapted to Quarto's HTML.

It does the following:

- Limiting the navbar to a centered, fixed-width container.
- Putting the navbar items (title, links, search, GitHub icon) in the same
  order as pkgdown.
- Styling the margin sidebar and reference index
  (`<dl class="ref-index">`) to look like their pkgdown counterparts.

There is one annoying thing that can't be fixed though: the navbar title does
not line up with the body text automatically. Quarto uses a different layout
for the home page, so the body's left edge is not in the same place on every page.
Therefore, the generated `quarto_website.yml` includes a small
`include-after-body` script that measures the actual offset after the page has
loaded and adjusts the navbar padding accordingly.
